title: WoW Launched 22 Years Ago Today With No Battlegrounds
hook: World of Warcraft went live on November 23, 2004 with no battlegrounds and no honor points, so players invented the endless Tarren Mill vs Southshore war, and ten years later Blizzard made it an official battleground. Did you ever get caught in it?
script: Did you know World of Warcraft launched without a single battleground? The game went live in the United States on this very day back in two thousand four, so today is its anniversary. If you wanted to fight the other faction, you had to find them in the open world. Players did exactly that. Two enemy towns, Alliance Southshore and Horde Tarren Mill, sat close enough that raids rolled back and forth for hours. Nobody could win. There was no scoreboard, no flag, and no honor points at all. Blizzard only added the first honor system in the spring of two thousand five. One month later, in June, a patch finally brought the first real battlegrounds, Warsong Gulch and Alterac Valley. The fights at Tarren Mill became a legend anyway. For the tenth anniversary in November of two thousand fourteen, Blizzard turned them into an official team deathmatch battleground, this time with a clear winner. Winning gave you the title Tarren Mill Terror or Southshore Slayer. The same event brought back the forty player Molten Core raid and handed every player a Molten Corgi pet. All of that grew out of a fight nobody at Blizzard designed. Did you ever get caught in the Tarren Mill wars? Follow for more gaming history.
